title: Introduce Toolcall Conductor with Async Signal Latching and OpenAI-compatible Result Hydration
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers increasingly run multi-tool workflows where the model issues parallel function/tool calls and expects deterministic result composition, streaming stability, and graceful retries. Motivation: previous ad-hoc orchestration led to gibberish structured outputs, duplicate side-effects when retries happened, and brittle OpenAI-compat behavior for function-calling sequences. This PR introduces a new lightweight Toolcall Conductor that centralizes execution ergonomics: async signal latching to coordinate parallel tool runs, idempotent result hydration to prevent duplicate injections, and an OpenAI-compat shim for function-calling semantics in streamed responses. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: add redwood/pkg/runtime/toolcall/conductor.go implementing a conductor that tracks call IDs, latches result signals, and emits ordered hydration events to the streaming layer. 2) api: update redwood/pkg/api/openai_compat/handlers.go to translate OpenAI-style function_call choices into conductor jobs and to consume conductor hydration events for stable streamed structured output. 3) sdk: small ergonomics helpers in redwood-sdk-python/redwood/tooling.py and redwood-sdk-typescript/src/tooling.ts to expose a non-blocking call API that wires into the conductor. 4) client compat tests and e2e flows in benchmark-lab/test/toolcall_conductor_test.go and redwood-examples/multi-tool-orchestration/ to demonstrate retry-safe replay. 5) docs: new section in redwood-docs/reference/tool-calling.md describing the conductor lifecycle and recommended retry semantics. Key behavior & guarantees: - Async Signal Latching: parallel tool executions post a transient signal with a stable ID; the conductor latches the first successful result per signal ID and deduplicates subsequent completions. - Idempotent Result Hydration: hydration objects are stamped with stable request-call identifiers and replay-safe tokens so retries or replays will not cause duplicate injections or side-effects. - Streaming Stability: the OpenAI-compat shim buffers partial tool outputs and emits structured function_call + response blocks in the same ordering across initial stream and any reconnects. - Retry policy: default hedged-retry policy with configurable window; retries for non-idempotent tools are disabled by default and require opt-in via tool metadata. Migration notes: minor SDK change for tool registration signature (opt-in param "idempotent": true/false) and server-side default policy; existing tool integrations continue to work but will not get automatic retries until annotated. Backward compatibility: OpenAI-compat endpoints remain backwards-compatible for single-tool calls; multi-tool streaming semantics improved but explicit opt-in required in some edge cases. Checklist: - [x] Implement conductor core and unit tests - [x] Integrate with OpenAI-compat handler - [x] Add SDK ergonomics helpers and examples - [x] Add regression tests for retries and replay - [x] Update docs and migration guide Testing: unit tests for latch/dedup logic, integration tests covering streaming reconnection scenarios, manual QA on Dedicated and Hosted with synthetic multi-tool workloads, load tests in perf pipeline to validate latency impact. Risk & mitigations: potential perf overhead from conductor coordination under extreme fan-out; mitigated with batching windows and fast-path bypass for single-tool calls. Non-idempotent tools present risk of duplicate side-effects; default policy disables retries and docs + SDK require explicit idempotent flag. Related work: follow-ups expected to add observability hooks in Redwood Console for per-call idempotency rates and latency heatmaps. review_comments: Jin Park: Nice clear separation between latching and hydration. Can we add a short-circuit single-tool fast path in the conductor to avoid locking on the common case?
Maya Patel: Added fast-path in conductor.go; benchmark shows <2% p99 impact for single-tool flows.
Luis Gomez: Suggest exposing idempotent flag in TS SDK as named option rather than positional arg for ergonomics.
Maya Patel: Updated TS SDK surface and added migration note in docs.
Ava Chen: CI flake on integration e2e, reran and passed. Consider adding a test for two concurrent identical signals to prove dedupe.
Maya Patel: Added concurrent-identical-signal test and asserted single hydration event.
Security review (Luis Gomez): Confirmed no new secrets surfaced; audit hooks added for all conductor decisions.
release_notes: Introduce Toolcall Conductor: centralized orchestration for multi-tool calls that provides async signal latching, idempotent result hydration, and improved OpenAI-compatible streaming for multi-tool workflows. SDKs add optional idempotent flag. Default policies disable retries for non-idempotent tools. See migration guide in docs.
testing: Unit tests cover latch/dedupe/retry policy. Integration tests simulate streaming reconnects and parallel tool invocations. Load tests validated latency impact under synthetic fan-out.
notes: This is intended as an incremental rollout; feature gated behind runtime flag and opt-in per-tenant configuration. Follow-up PRs will add console metrics and finer-grained routing by cost tier.
